decisions.why: Text unchanged; FR-001 asks for the contract's own voice and no longer than the check needs.

decisions.why: FR-007 names that test module and FR-009 asks for a make target; the escape is the repository's own route for an edit the spec demands. Unchanged by Amendment 2, which edits the same test module again under the same line.

decisions.summary: The Route line stays DIRECT although the amendments' delta reaches the skill Makefile, the tier test and scripts/.
decisions.why: The route is chosen from the delta by the repository's rule - engine code is l7r/**/*.py and pool/*.gen.py|*.json - and none of the amendment paths are engine code. The Route line's enumeration is incomplete as prose; the decision it records is unchanged and correct.

decisions.summary: The Constitution Check's XVI line now reads 'the field is set on all twelve agents in every case (FR-002, FR-004) - no exception at the first landing; Amendment 2's P10 carries the GM's one exception, spec-fidelity, named in the tier test'.
decisions.why: New text since the previous verdict. It decides nothing; it restates the spec's own history. Checked true in both halves: the spec's Status line records that at the first landing the field was set in all twelve, and FR-013 excepts spec-fidelity alone thereafter with the tier test naming it. The line no longer misstates the shipped state, which the unamended 'no exception' did.

decisions.summary: One test in the tier-test module, test_every_agent_launches_without_the_claude_md_files, requiring the field of every file in the already-derived roster, its message naming the field, the GM's ruling and the feature; the module docstring gains the ruling; the tier table is untouched.
decisions.why: FR-007 word for word as it then read. FR-013 later narrows its scope by one named agent, and P10 records that change; P6's text describes Amendment 1's work at the time it was done and is not contradicted by the shipped test, which still derives its roster from the directory and still requires the field of every file the exception table does not name.

decisions.summary: The guard is proven by removing the field from one file and watching the test go red, and root CLAUDE.md's gate row for the tier test gains a clause naming what it now enforces.
decisions.why: The red proof is FR-007's second sentence verbatim. The gate row is a one-clause documentation edit to a row that already exists for that file; P10 keeps it true, and it now reads 'omitClaudeMd on every agent file but the one the test names'.

decisions.summary: spec-fidelity.md question 4's 'extra verification the GM did not request' becomes 'verification of something the GM did not ask for', with a paragraph after question 5 stating the distinction on this feature's round 1 as the worked example; spec-fidelity-verify.md gains the same paragraph.
decisions.why: FR-008 asks that BOTH fidelity contracts carry the GM's distinction and identifies question 4's phrase as the sentence that caused the cut.

decisions.why: FR-008's own sentence, and the repository's stated method for improving a review agent. Amendment 2 does not reopen the method: FR-012 accepts the change with SC-007 recorded unmet, which is a ruling on the RESULT of this run, not a change to it.

decisions.summary: make scatter-bases MAP=<pool map> in the skill Makefile (GUARD_EDIT_OK, a read-only diagnostic) and settlement-review's paragraph names the target; the three (Tools: ...) tails cut; the seven contracts citing the tier test cite its real path.

The plan leaves HOW the recipe reaches parse_bases open; the shipped work routes it through scripts/_scatter_bases.py with its own tests, which is still within FR-009 and still not recorded in the plan text - prose, not a decision to do otherwise.

decisions.summary: The six agents with recorded runs are paired on named recorded cases, each cut to a slice the record already scored.
decisions.why: FR-010 asks for exactly these six 'each on one recorded case with known findings'. Amendment 2 does not reopen the roster: spec-fidelity's pair is what produced the evidence the GM's second ruling rests on.

decisions.summary: building-review on tests/fixtures/ochiba-no-scale-red.svg and size-audit on tests/fixtures/ochiba-big-bath-red.svg, each staged in a HEAD worktree beside a copy of the Ochiba notes and rendered to PNG.

decisions.summary: All eight pairs run by FR-003's harness and rule with FR-004 governing a miss; sixteen runs; settlement-review and perf-audit priced in research.md with their reasons.
decisions.why: FR-010's own words. The pricing reached the GM as the third of the three questions in request.md's third block, which is what 'put to the GM ... not decided by the session' asked for, and the GM ruled on it (FR-014).

decisions.summary: T07 -> T08 -> T09 -> T10 -> T11 for Amendment 1.
decisions.why: It follows FR-007 to FR-011 in order; tasks.md T07-T11 name the same work with the same requirement ids.

decisions.summary: No new machinery for Amendment 2; P7's paragraph in both fidelity contracts gains the test-versus-guard sentence in place.
decisions.why: FR-012 asks for exactly this, in the same change and in both contracts: a test that only FAILS when the requested thing is absent is verification; a guard that REFUSES, BLOCKS or REWRITES is behavior. R7 records the run that showed the first wording let a refusing guard through, which is the sentence's stated reason.

decisions.summary: omitClaudeMd is deleted from spec-fidelity.md alone, so eleven of the twelve agents launch without the CLAUDE.md files and the memory index instead of all twelve.
decisions.why: It narrows the GM's 2026-09-19 ruling that a DEFINED subagent should not be handed those files, and narrows FR-007's guard, so it is adjudicated rather than waved through. It is the GM's own carve-out in their own words, not a session's: request.md's third block puts the choice to the GM ('I can keep the field on or take it off for this one agent ... I recommend taking it off until a three-samples-per-leg test ... can tell field from variance') and the GM answered 'go with your recommendations to all three'. The size is exactly what was ruled - one named agent, not a class, not a criterion another agent could later meet - and it is time-bounded in the spec and in the record by the test that would end it (FR-013, research R8). Verified in the tree: spec-fidelity.md is the only agent file without the field, and the other eleven carry it.

decisions.summary: The tier test gains KEEPS_CLAUDE_MD, a name-to-reason table the guard skips and asserts is not stale, so the hole in FR-007's guard is the size of the ruling and cannot silently grow.
decisions.why: FR-013 settles the mechanism by name: 'the tier test carries the exception BY NAME with the ruling as its reason (KEEPS_CLAUDE_MD), and fails on a row that has gone stale'. Verified against the shipped test: KEEPS_CLAUDE_MD holds one row, spec-fidelity, whose value is the GM's ruling with its date and the evidence; wrong skips only names in that table; stale fails on a named agent that is gone or that carries the field after all. The claim that it cannot silently grow holds in the sense that matters - the table lives in a guard file, so a new row costs a GUARD_EDIT_OK with a reason, and the file's own comment records that an entry is the GM's ruling and never a session's convenience. Whether a future session could add a row it should not is that session's decision to justify, not one this plan makes.

decisions.summary: Root CLAUDE.md, the guard table's gate row, docs/efficiency-tooling.md and research.md R8 record the exception and what would end it.
decisions.why: These are the same records FR-006 and P5 already own, kept true after the field's reach changed, plus SC-010's requirement that research.md says what would put the field back. Verified: the root bullet names spec-fidelity alone with the GM's ruling of 2026-09-20; the gate row reads 'omitClaudeMd on every agent file but the one the test names'; the efficiency-tooling row carries the same; R8 names the three-samples-a-leg run at about four weight units by R6's per-run weights. No document outside those the spec names is touched.
